column3: The Hebrew actively says unnamed people reported the words, then that Saul took David. BSB uses passive “reported to Saul” and says Saul “called for him.”
The Hebrew uses “him” in the first clause and names “this Philistine” in the second; BSB names the Philistine first and then uses “him.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names Saul as the recipient and joins the lion and bear with “and”; BSB leaves the addressee implicit and uses “or.”
The Hebrew says David seized the animal by its “beard”; BSB renders this as “fur.”
The Hebrew has singular “the lion” and “the bear” and uses a verb for striking; BSB has plural “lions and bears” and uses “killed.”
The Hebrew repeats “hand” for the lion and the bear; BSB combines these as their “claws.”
The Hebrew calls the clothing “his garments” in the plural; BSB uses singular “his own tunic.”
The Hebrew twice uses the verb for testing or trying in explaining his difficulty walking; BSB renders both as being “not accustomed.” The garments are plural, where BSB has singular “tunic.”
The Hebrew leaves David unnamed and refers to the shepherds collectively in the plural. BSB supplies David and uses singular “his shepherd’s bag.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the speaker “the Philistine” in the first clause; BSB uses “he.”
The Hebrew again names the speaker “the Philistine”; BSB uses “he.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew describes a carcass of the Philistine camp collectively in the singular; BSB uses plural “carcasses of the Philistines.” The final statement says there is a God “for Israel,” where BSB has “in Israel.”
The Hebrew uses singular “our hand”; BSB uses plural “our hands.”
The Hebrew repeats David and the Philistine as the advancing parties; BSB replaces both with pronouns in parts of the verse.
The Hebrew explicitly says David sent his hand into the container; BSB compresses this to reaching into his bag.
The Hebrew repeats David’s name in the final statement about the sword; BSB refers to “his hand.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the slain Philistines “fell” along the road; BSB describes their bodies as being “strewn” there.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew refers to “his equipment” without repeating the Philistine’s name; BSB supplies “Goliath’s weapons.”
The Hebrew’s oath says “as your soul lives”; BSB leaves the soul image implicit in “As surely as you live.”
The Hebrew commands the hearer to “ask” whose son he is; BSB uses “Find out.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the head of the Philistine”; BSB uses “his head” and supplies “still.”
Close to the Hebrew.
